By 1998, financial constraints once again brought his racing ambition to a halt. In 2009, Zen Low, still burning with determination and drive in motorsports, transitioned to car racing after securing sufficient funding. The following year, in 2012, he finally broke the chain of bad fortune and claimed the national championship title in the Malaysia Super Series with seven podium finishes. creator: Melotick
disclosure: <!-- Do not remove this line! --> {{AfC comment|1=The French revision does not comply with [[WP:NOLLM]], so a translation thereof cannot comply with [[WP:LLMTRANSLATE]]. [[User:Kisseran|Kisseran]] ([[User talk:Kisseran|talk]]) 17:14, 10 November 2026 (UTC)}} {{AfC comment|1=In preparing this draft, I disclose that AI assistance was used as follows: {{Hidden begin}}nowiki{{LLM-assisted translation}} {{Short description|French harpsichordist and author (born 1960)}} {{Infobox musical artist | name = Olivier Baumont | background = non_vocal_instrumentalist | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1960|8|15|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Saint-Dié-des-Vosges]], France | instrument = [[Harpsichord]] | occupation = Harpsichordist, author, teacher | genre = [[Classical music]], [[Baroque music]] | website = {{URL|https://www.olivierbaumont.fr/}} }} '''Olivier Baumont''' (born 15 August 1960) is a French [[harpsichordist]], author and teacher. His career has focused particularly on French keyboard music of the 17th and 18th centuries. He has taught harpsichord at the [[Conservatoire de Paris]] since 2001 and has recorded the complete harpsichord works of [[François Couperin]], [[Jean-Philippe Rameau]] and [[Jacques Duphly]].<ref name="Larousse">{{cite encyclopedia |title=Olivier Baumont |encyclopedia=Dictionnaire de la musique |publisher=Larousse |url=https://www.larousse.fr/encyclopedie/musdico/Olivier_Baumont/166144 |language=fr }}</ref><ref name="CNSMDP">{{cite web |title=Olivier Baumont |url=https://www.conservatoiredeparis.fr/fr/enseignant/baumont-olivier |website=Conservatoire de Paris |language=fr |access-date=10 November 2026 }}</ref> == Biography == === Early life and education === Born in [[Saint-Dié-des-Vosges]], France, Baumont began studying the harpsichord at the conservatory in [[Annecy]]. He continued his studies at the [[Conservatoire de Paris]], where he obtained first prizes in harpsichord and chamber music in 1981 and 1982. He subsequently studied with [[Huguette Dreyfus]] and [[Kenneth Gilbert]], and attended interpretation classes given by [[Gustav Leonhardt]] in Cologne, Germany.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> In 1982, he won the Radio France soloists' competition and made his first recording.<ref name="Larousse"/> === Musical career === Baumont has performed in recitals and chamber music concerts throughout France and internationally. He has appeared at the Ambronay Festival, the [[Festival de La Roque-d'Anthéron]], the Radio France and Montpellier Festival and events organised by the Centre de musique baroque de Versailles. His performances have also taken him to Japan, the United States, Canada, South America and various European countries.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> In the early 1990s, he became artistic director of the Festival Couperin, originally held in [[Chaumes-en-Brie]] and subsequently in [[Champs-sur-Marne]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Festival Couperin |url=https://www.lexpress.fr/informations/festival-couperin_595850.html |work=L'Express |date=23 September 1993 |language=fr }}</ref> He has collaborated with musicians including [[Davitt Moroney]], [[Jean-Paul Fouchécourt]], [[Hugo Reyne]], [[Christophe Coin]] and [[Julien Chauvin (violinist)|Julien Chauvin]]. In March 2014, Baumont initiated a series at the [[Cité de la musique]] in Paris devoted to the complete harpsichord works of [[Johann Sebastian Bach]]. The project brought together twenty harpsichordists of different generations and featured historical instruments.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> === Teaching and music research === In September 2001, Baumont was appointed professor of harpsichord at the [[Conservatoire de Paris]], where he has also taught continuo playing.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> Alongside his teaching, he gives masterclasses and lectures on historical performance practice and the French Baroque repertoire. His research has included editing and restoring keyboard music by composers such as [[Michel Corrette]], [[Jacques Duphly]] and Francis Thomé. He has also appeared on radio and television programmes devoted to classical music, including broadcasts on [[France Musique]], [[France Culture]], the BBC and Mezzo. === Theatre and cinema === Baumont's work has extended beyond the concert stage to theatre, literature and cinema. He adapted [[Denis Diderot]]'s ''[[Rameau's Nephew]]'' for the theatre. The production was performed in Paris, notably at the Théâtre Le Ranelagh, with actors Nicolas Vaude and Nicolas Marié, before touring. In 2016, he contributed the music for ''[[A Woman's Life (film)|A Woman's Life]]'' (''Une vie''), directed by [[Stéphane Brizé]] and based on the novel by [[Guy de Maupassant]]. The film's music draws in part on 18th-century keyboard works, including compositions by Jacques Duphly.<ref>{{cite web |title=Une vie |url=https://diaphana.fr/film/une-vie/ |website=Diaphana Distribution |language=fr }}</ref> Baumont has also performed with the French actor [[Denis Podalydès]] in literary concerts combining readings and harpsichord music, particularly around the works of [[Marcel Proust]].<ref name="Franciscaines">{{cite web |title=Olivier Baumont |url=https://festivallitterairedeauville.fr/fr/artistes/olivier-baumont |website=Les Franciscaines |language=fr }}</ref> === Recordings === Baumont has recorded a substantial repertoire of Baroque keyboard music. His discography includes the complete harpsichord works of [[Jean-Philippe Rameau]] and [[François Couperin]], as well as recordings devoted to [[Johann Sebastian Bach]], [[Henry Purcell]], [[George Frideric Handel]] and [[Georg Philipp Telemann]]. He has also recorded music by [[Jacques Champion de Chambonnières]], [[Louis-Claude Daquin]], [[Jean-François Dandrieu]] and [[Claude Balbastre]]. In 2022, he released ''Un clavecin pour Marcel Proust'', an album associated with the musical world of the French novelist, marking the centenary of Proust's death. In 2024, Plectra Music released his recording of works by [[Michel Corrette]], entitled ''Les Amants Enchantés & Other Harpsichord Pieces''. In 2026, Baumont released a complete recording of [[Jacques Duphly]]'s harpsichord works on the Plectra Music label. Recorded on historical harpsichords from the Flint Collection in the United States, the three-disc set comprises all 52 of Duphly's harpsichord pieces. The recording was reviewed by François Ekchajzer in ''[[Télérama]]'' in August 2026.<ref name="Duphly2026">{{cite magazine |last=Ekchajzer |first=François |title=Complete Works for Harpsichord : Jacques Duphly d'Olivier Baumont : notre critique |url=https://www.telerama.fr/musique/complete-works-for-harpsichord-jacques-duphly-d-olivier-baumont-notre-critique_cri-7045559.php |magazine=Télérama |date=25 August 2026 |language=fr }}</ref> === Writing and literary activities === In addition to his musical career, Baumont has published several books on French musical history, literature and the relationship between music and the arts. In 1998, he published ''Couperin, le musicien des rois'' in the [[Découvertes Gallimard]] collection. The book received the Prix des Muses that year.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> His 2007 book ''La Musique à Versailles'', published by Actes Sud in collaboration with the Palace of Versailles and the Centre de musique baroque de Versailles, received an award from the French music critics' association.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> He later published ''À l'Opéra, monsieur ! La musique dans les Mémoires de Saint-Simon'' (Gallimard, 2015) and ''Tombeau du jeune monsieur de Cinq-Mars'' (Arléa, 2021). In 2024, he published his first novel, ''D'une partition m'apparaissait un dessin'', with Bleu nuit. The novel was shortlisted for the 2025 Prix Livres & Musiques, awarded at Les Franciscaines in Deauville.<ref name="Franciscaines"/> === Residencies at Chambord === Baumont has maintained an artistic association with the [[Château de Chambord]], where he has performed concerts and undertaken several writing residencies. His first two residencies contributed to the development of ''À l'Opéra, monsieur !'' and ''Tombeau du jeune monsieur de Cinq-Mars''. In 2026, he undertook a third writing residency at Chambord to research a book on the history of music at the château, from the Renaissance to the present day. The project examines the role of music in the château's history, including court entertainments, theatre, religious ceremonies, hunting traditions and later artistic performances.<ref name="Chambord2026">{{cite web |title=Résidence d'artiste – Olivier Baumont |url=https://www.chambord.org/fr/residence-dartiste-olivier-baumont/ |website=Domaine national de Chambord |year=2026 |language=fr |access-date=10 November 2026 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Rencontre hors-les-murs – Artistes en circuit-court – Olivier Baumont |url=https://www.chambord.org/fr/post/rencontres-hors-les-murs-artistes-en-circuit-court-olivier-baumont/ |website=Domaine national de Chambord |year=2026 |language=fr }}</ref> == Publications == * Baumont, Olivier.
